Theme

School & learning

biological adjective

also biologically, biology, biologist, biological mother, biological father, biological parents, birth mother

modern

Traupman 279

biologicus, biologica, biologicum

adjective, declension

biological, of biology

Traupman’s word, with biologia, biology, and biologus, a biologist (Traupman 279). For “living, natural” in a general sense, Latin uses vīvus or nātūrālis.

Other words

  • nātūrālis, nātūrāle — biological (of a parent), by birth

    adjective, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Phil. 3.15: nātūrālis pater, opposed to the adoptive father (Lewis & Short); Liv. 42.52 (Lewis & Short)

    Of a father, a son, a grandson: by birth, not by adoption. Its general sense is “natural” (see natural).

Examples

  • Pater ejus nātūrālis in Graeciā vīvit.

    His biological father lives in Greece.composed

See also life, nature, natural.

SourcesLewis & Short: naturalis

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 279.
